scope: Actual UiOutputOriginal.EnterOutput, ObserveOutput, AcceptedOwnerCurrent, ResumeUiOutput, FinishUiOutputInventoryResume, BeginUiOutputCachedResume and ConsumeUiOutputCachedPrimary composed with the whole actual native-order inventory predictor. Native item/container behavior, source-current qualification, publication, native helper/callback execution and setters are explicit adapters.
cases: Original primary entry publishes its expected native owner result before a setter runs.
Expected actual primary result advances exactly one accepted prefix; the ordered extra follows it.
A different primary cannot borrow the original application.
A native true return without the expected owner result cannot advance.
A changed owner prefix prevents entry of the next output.
A native refusal or changed source scope cannot publish accepted progress.
The same retained source continues only remaining extras after its accepted primary without repeating the primary.
Returned application, unobserved native entry and changed accepted owner image cannot replay a prefix.
Native false with complete unchanged owner preimage saves a refusal and permits a distinct remaining-extra retry; changed grids and failed refusal publication remain latched.
Repeated explicit refusals retain distinct create-only attempt records without accepted progress.
A positively refused original primary can retry its already generated value then extras without repeating effects; absent accepted progress and absent positive refusal cannot enter recovery.
Armor false remains latched despite equal final owner images because native equipment callbacks may already have fired.
Actual cached inventory retry retains the scope and acknowledges the exact previously accepted primary once, allowing native callback and queue progress without another insertion.

A workstation grid cannot borrow this inventory-only cached route. A complete physical prefix may invoke its still-unentered native callback once without another insertion; an entered callback without positive return remains held.
limitations: Thirty authored assertions, not run. Includes actual warm native-helper continuation and entered/returned/no-repeat handling with an explicit native helper dispatch/callback adapter. Does not prove native outputStack/giveExp integration, filesystem atomic publication, actual native setters, native saved player prefixes, replacement-card or cold continuation, installed native callback composition, native queue decrement or multiplayer topology.
